issues.legal_issue: The market value of a large agricultural acquisition may be assessed by reference to small-plot sales only with appropriate adjustments for differences in size, use, and development requirements.
material_facts: A large area of agricultural land was acquired for providing house sites.
The claimants relied on nearby sale instances involving small plots, including a sale of 162 square yards at Rs. 82 per square yard.
The High Court used that sale as a comparable, deducted one-third for development, and fixed compensation at Rs. 55 per square yard.
The acquired agricultural land required development for roads and civic amenities before use as house sites.
issues.conclusion: Small-plot sale prices are not ordinarily a safe measure for valuing a large acquired area, but may be considered where appropriate, with necessary adjustments. Applying a 53% deduction to the relied-upon sale value, the Court fixed compensation at approximately Rs. 40 per square yard and allowed the appeals to that extent.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 23, 24 and 25 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, compensation is determined by the land’s market value on the date of publication of the Section 4(1) notification, subject to the statutory matters to be considered and excluded and the statutory minimum. Market value is assessed by reference to what a willing vendor and willing purchaser might reasonably agree, without treating either as compelled. Comparable sales should be reasonably close in time, bona fide, relate to the acquired land or adjacent land, and involve similar advantages. Small-plot sales are generally not a safe guide for a large acquisition, though they may be used where appropriate material is otherwise unavailable, after suitable deductions. Development deductions depend on the circumstances and may account for land needed for roads and amenities, development expenses, deferred realization and venture profits. The Court relied on The Collector of Lakhimour v. Bhuban Chandra Dutta; Prithvi Raj Taneja v. State of Madhya Pradesh; Kausalya Devi Bogra v. Land Acquisition Officer; Suresh Kumar v. Town Improvement Trust, Bhopal; Vyricherla Narayana Gajapatiraju v. Revenue Divisional Officer, Vizagapatam; Special Land Acquisition Officer, Bangalore v. T. Adinarayan Setty; Administrator General of West Bengal v. Collector, Varanasi; Brig. Sahib Singh Kalha v. Amritsar Improvement Trust; and K.S. Shivadevamma v. Assistant Commissioner and Land Acquisition Officer.

rule.if: land_acquisition_compensation_appeal and large_agricultural_tract_acquired and small_plot_sale_used_as_comparator and development_required

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_appeal: An appeal concerns the amount of compensation payable for land acquired for a public purpose.
predicates.large_agricultural_tract_acquired: A substantial tract of land that was agricultural was acquired.
predicates.small_plot_sale_used_as_comparator: A party relied on the sale price of a small plot to support the valuation of the acquired land.
predicates.development_required: The acquired land required development, including provision for roads or civic amenities, before its intended use.

issues.definition: When a compensation appeal concerns a large agricultural tract valued using a small-plot sale and development is required, the market value is fixed after an appropriate development deduction.
